title: Quantum Research
subtitle: A reference for quantum science and information

chapters.title: Quantum Foundations
chapters.summary: The mathematical and conceptual foundations of quantum states, measurement, correlations, and dynamics.
paragraphs: Quantum foundations studies the mathematical and conceptual assumptions of quantum mechanics. Principal questions concern the representation of physical states, the measurement process, the structure of correlations, and the relation between quantum and classical descriptions.

Operational predictions and their interpretation are distinct objects of study. Bell inequalities constrain local hidden-variable explanations of correlations. Decoherence and open-system models describe the influence of an environment on observable interference and reduced dynamics.

sections.title: Measurement and nonlocality
sections.summary: Quantum measurement, Bell inequalities, and the assumptions underlying local hidden-variable models.
paragraphs: Quantum measurement assigns outcome probabilities to a specified state and measurement procedure. For composite systems, joint outcome distributions can violate Bell inequalities that hold for local hidden-variable models under the stated independence assumptions.

Research concerns the characterization of allowed correlations, experimental tests of nonlocality, and the assumptions required for statistical inference. Decoherence describes suppression of interference through environmental interaction; it does not by itself resolve the interpretation of individual measurement outcomes.

sections.title: Device-independent certification
sections.summary: Certification of quantum states and measurements from observed correlations, with explicit statistical and physical assumptions.
paragraphs: Device-independent certification infers properties of quantum states or measurements from observed correlations without requiring a detailed model of the devices. Guarantees remain conditional on assumptions about the experimental arrangement, independence of settings, and the applicability of quantum theory.

Self-testing identifies states and measurements up to equivalences that cannot be distinguished from the observed statistics. Research addresses robust bounds, finite-sample analysis, and the measurement complexity of certifying larger systems.
questions: How tight can certification guarantees remain with finite samples and imperfect correlations?
How can protocols certify larger systems without an impractical measurement burden?

chapters.title: Open quantum systems
chapters.summary: Reduced dynamics, quantum channels, dissipation, and the validity of Markovian approximations.
paragraphs: Open quantum systems interact with environmental degrees of freedom. Their local statistics are described by reduced density operators. Under appropriate preparation assumptions, quantum channels represent the evolution between specified times.

Continuous-time descriptions include master equations and more general models with memory. Research examines the validity of weak-coupling and Markovian approximations, the reconstruction of reduced dynamics, and the role of system-environment correlations in prediction and control.

sections.title: Non-Markovian quantum processes
sections.summary: Temporal correlations, non-Markovian dynamics, and the reconstruction of multi-time quantum processes.
paragraphs: When a system remains correlated with its environment, its later behavior can depend on earlier interventions. Comparing states at only two times may not capture all of that dependence.

Multi-time process descriptions organize both the dynamics and the experimental operations used to probe it. Research must balance expressive models against the number of measurements and computational resources needed to reconstruct them.
questions: Which memory features can be identified with a tractable number of interventions?
How can a reduced model retain the memory relevant to prediction or control?

chapters.title: Quantum Information Theory
chapters.summary: Entanglement, quantum channels, resource theories, and limits on quantum information processing.
paragraphs: Quantum information theory studies information encoded in quantum states and processed through quantum operations. It characterizes state distinguishability, entanglement, communication rates, and transformations under specified resource constraints.

Operational tasks provide definitions of quantities such as channel capacity and distillable entanglement. Research seeks achievable protocols, converse bounds, and computable characterizations, including finite-resource settings and correlated noise.

sections.title: Entanglement and quantum communication
sections.summary: Entanglement detection, conversion, and its use in quantum communication protocols.
paragraphs: Entanglement is a property of a composite quantum state. Its operational value depends on the allowed local operations, available classical communication, and the protocol under consideration.

Teleportation illustrates the distinction: transferring an unknown state requires both shared entanglement and classical communication. Long-distance networking adds physical constraints such as loss, finite memory lifetimes, and imperfect operations.

sections.title: Entanglement resource theory
sections.summary: Detection, quantification, and conversion of bipartite and multipartite entanglement.
paragraphs: Entanglement resource theory characterizes states and their transformations relative to a specified class of allowed operations. Detection establishes whether entanglement is present; quantification and conversion address the rates or costs of particular information-processing tasks.

Research includes mixed-state and multipartite entanglement, computable bounds on conversion rates, and relations between resource measures and experimentally accessible witnesses. The relevant measure depends on the operational task and available resources.
questions: Which experimentally accessible quantities give useful bounds on entanglement-assisted tasks?
How can conversion and distribution of multipartite entanglement be characterized with manageable resources?

sections.title: Quantum channels and communication limits
sections.summary: Achievable communication rates and capacity bounds for noisy quantum channels.
paragraphs: A quantum channel describes a physical transformation of quantum states. A capacity expresses an achievable communication rate under specified resources, error criteria, and assumptions about repeated uses of that transformation.

The challenge is to connect these operational definitions with quantities that can actually be computed or bounded. Correlated noise and finite-use settings require care because familiar memoryless and asymptotic descriptions need not capture them.
questions: Which bounds remain useful for finite uses of channels with memory?
How can tractable channel models retain the noise correlations relevant to communication?

chapters.title: Quantum Computing
chapters.summary: Quantum algorithms, computational complexity, simulation, and fault-tolerant computation.
paragraphs: Quantum computing studies how physical evolution can perform a computation and what resources that computation requires. Its theoretical questions concern algorithm design, simulation, complexity, and the protection of logical information.

Algorithms and error correction form complementary branches: one concerns the procedure for solving a problem; the other concerns its reliability under imperfect operations. Programming research addresses representation and execution, while processor technologies address physical integration.

sections.title: Algorithms and quantum simulation
sections.summary: Quantum algorithm design, simulation methods, and computational resource analysis.
paragraphs: Algorithm research studies the resources required to produce an answer: operations, measurements, precision, input preparation, and classical processing. A meaningful comparison specifies these resources on both the quantum and classical sides.

Quantum simulation uses a controllable quantum system to investigate another system. Hybrid methods combine quantum evaluations with classical optimization, making the costs and reliability of that loop part of the scientific question.

sections.title: Variational quantum algorithms
sections.summary: Trainability, sampling complexity, and noise sensitivity of variational quantum algorithms.
paragraphs: A variational algorithm adjusts a circuit by repeatedly estimating an objective and updating parameters with a classical optimizer. Its success depends on more than circuit expressiveness: noise, sampling, initialization, and the optimization landscape all matter.

Performance analysis requires explicit noise models, measurement budgets, optimization costs, and classical comparison methods. Numerical results on small instances do not establish asymptotic speedup; scaling claims require separate complexity analysis.
questions: Which circuit structures make learning or optimization feasible as a problem grows?
When measurement and optimization costs are included, which tasks remain competitive with strong classical methods?

chapters.title: Quantum error correction
chapters.summary: Quantum codes, syndrome measurement, decoding, and fault-tolerant logical operations.
paragraphs: An error-correcting code stores logical information in a subspace of several physical systems. Carefully chosen measurements reveal information about errors while avoiding a direct measurement of the protected logical state.

Fault tolerance extends this idea to imperfect operations, measurements, and recovery procedures. Code properties, connectivity, and decoding all contribute to the practical cost. Different code families make different tradeoffs.

sections.title: Scalable fault-tolerant computation
sections.summary: Logical error rates, gate implementation, and resource requirements for scalable fault-tolerant computation.
paragraphs: A logical memory tests how well encoded information survives repeated error-correction cycles. A useful processor must additionally prepare, operate on, and read out logical states without losing that protection.

Below-threshold memory results are important evidence for scaling, but complete computation brings further challenges: correlated errors, leakage, decoding latency, and the resources needed for logical gates.
questions: How does logical performance change when protected operations replace idle memory cycles?
How can decoding, calibration, and control keep pace with a growing processor?

sections.title: Quantum low-density parity-check codes
sections.summary: Quantum low-density parity-check codes, decoding algorithms, and implementation overhead.
paragraphs: Quantum low-density parity-check codes use sparse sets of checks to constrain errors. Some constructions offer attractive encoding rates, but code parameters alone do not determine whether an implementation is practical.

Research combines mathematical code design with syndrome circuits, connectivity, decoding, and logical operations. Comparisons must use compatible noise models and account for the full implementation rather than only stored qubits.
questions: Which low-overhead constructions remain favorable after routing and syndrome extraction are included?
How can efficient decoding and a useful set of logical operations be realized together?

chapters.title: Quantum matter and simulation platforms
chapters.summary: Interacting quantum systems, phases of matter, and controlled platforms for quantum simulation.
paragraphs: When many quantum degrees of freedom interact, collective behavior emerges that is not evident from one isolated constituent. Correlations, phases, and dynamics connect condensed-matter questions to quantum information.
Controlled platforms make selected models experimentally accessible. The challenge is to determine which features of a model survive preparation, control, readout, and finite system size.

sections.title: Many-body dynamics
sections.summary: Entanglement dynamics, transport, relaxation, and measurement in interacting quantum systems.
paragraphs: Many-body dynamics studies what happens when an interacting system evolves, is driven, or is measured. The growth of entanglement connects this physics to both the difficulty of classical simulation and the possibilities of quantum experiments.

Measurement is itself an intervention. Repeated observations can compete with entangling dynamics, so the measurement protocol becomes part of the model rather than simply a passive way to inspect it.

sections.title: Measurement-induced quantum phases
sections.summary: Entanglement transitions in monitored many-body systems and their experimental signatures.
paragraphs: In monitored many-body systems, coherent dynamics can create entanglement while measurements reshape or remove it. Varying the monitoring can lead to qualitatively different patterns of entanglement in individual measurement-conditioned evolutions.

Connecting these theoretical distinctions to experiments requires suitable observables and careful treatment of finite size, postselection, and device noise. These issues connect monitored dynamics to statistical mechanics and quantum information theory.
questions: Which signatures distinguish a transition from a finite-size or noise-induced crossover?
How can measurement-conditioned phenomena be probed without prohibitive data or postselection costs?

chapters.title: Characterization and experimental validation
chapters.summary: Estimation and validation of quantum states, operations, and device noise from experimental data.
paragraphs: Characterization connects experimental records to a model of a state, operation, or device. The chosen protocol determines which properties can be estimated and which assumptions are needed to interpret them.

Average gate error does not determine the full noise process. Experimental validation combines a suitable protocol with uncertainty estimates, checks for drift, and comparisons against independently motivated predictions.

sections.title: Benchmarking under realistic noise
sections.summary: Device benchmarking with correlated errors, drift, and context-dependent noise.
paragraphs: Benchmarking summarizes the behavior of an operation or device through a specified experiment. Its result is useful only to the extent that the experiment and its assumptions capture the behavior relevant to the intended task.

Research addresses statistically efficient detection of departures from assumed noise models. Different metrics can be complementary; a favorable average value does not by itself establish reliable performance for every computation.
questions: How can limited data distinguish slow drift, correlated errors, and sampling fluctuations?
Which benchmark quantities predict performance on a specified application or logical operation?

chapters.title: Quantum languages and software systems
chapters.summary: Quantum programming languages, intermediate representations, semantics, and compiler correctness.
paragraphs: Quantum programming languages and intermediate representations specify operations on quantum states together with measurement and classical control. Their semantics define program behavior and the equivalences that a compiler must preserve.

Research addresses expressive language design, efficient representation, optimization, and verification. Hardware-specific compilation adds constraints on supported operations, connectivity, and timing; these constraints must be incorporated without invalidating the program specification.

sections.title: Hardware-aware compilation and routing
sections.summary: Circuit decomposition, qubit mapping, and routing under hardware constraints.
paragraphs: A circuit may specify interactions that a physical processor cannot perform directly. Compilation decomposes operations and assigns logical qubits to physical locations, adding routing operations when required.

The research problem is to optimize a meaningful cost while respecting correctness and device restrictions. Gate count, depth, execution time, and estimated error can favor different implementations, so benchmark conditions must be explicit.
questions: Which cost models predict execution quality across varying device conditions?
How can mapping and routing scale while retaining useful guarantees or strong comparison baselines?

sections.title: Quantum program verification
sections.summary: Formal specifications, equivalence checking, and correctness proofs for quantum programs.
paragraphs: Program verification relates an implementation to a precise statement of its intended behavior. For circuits, it can establish that a transformation preserves the represented computation instead of relying solely on example executions.

Research addresses the scalability of specifications, proof construction, and proof maintenance. A verified transformation only establishes the properties represented in its formal model; physical device behavior requires additional evidence.
questions: How can verification handle richer measurement and classical-control behavior at useful scales?
How should approximate optimizations state and compose their correctness guarantees?

sections.title: Reproducible hybrid quantum workflows
sections.summary: Execution models, data provenance, and reproducibility of quantum-classical computations.
paragraphs: A hybrid workflow combines circuit generation, quantum evaluations, classical optimization, and analysis. Software behavior depends on the interaction of these stages, not solely on the mathematical algorithm at its center.

Programming research asks how to preserve experiment configuration, measurement conventions, numerical settings, and provenance across implementations. Reproducibility requires specifications of simulator settings, device configurations, and execution environments.
questions: Which execution records are sufficient to reproduce and explain a hybrid result?
How can equivalent workflows be tested across different circuit representations and target environments?

chapters.title: Quantum Communication and Networks
chapters.summary: Physical links, quantum memories, and network protocols for distributing quantum information.
paragraphs: Quantum communication technology concerns the physical realization of protocols between separated systems. Sources, channels, memories, and local operations jointly determine the quality and rate of the distributed quantum resource.

Network research combines these components into architectures that tolerate loss, limited memory lifetimes, and uncertain link generation. The underlying entanglement and communication limits are studied in Quantum Information Theory; this branch concerns their realization at a system level.

sections.title: Quantum repeaters and network scaling
sections.summary: Quantum repeater protocols, entanglement distribution, and resource allocation in quantum networks.
paragraphs: A quantum repeater architecture divides a long communication task into smaller operations, combining distributed entanglement, memories, and appropriate error-management procedures. An unknown quantum state cannot simply be copied and amplified like a classical signal.
The research problem is architectural as well as physical. Link generation, memory duration, local processing, and scheduling must work together to achieve a useful end-to-end rate and quality.
questions: Which architecture gives a useful rate when losses, memory decay, and local errors are counted together?
How should a network allocate limited memories and schedule probabilistic links?

chapters.title: Quantum sensing and metrology
chapters.summary: Quantum parameter estimation, sensor design, and precision bounds under physical resource constraints.
paragraphs: A quantum sensor turns an unknown physical quantity into a change in a quantum state. Preparation, signal interaction, control, and readout jointly determine what can be learned.
Metrology asks how precisely a parameter can be estimated under a specified resource budget. A fair comparison includes time, repetitions, state preparation, and noise, not only an ideal sensitivity.

sections.title: Estimation, control, and noise
sections.summary: Statistical estimation and quantum control in the presence of measurement uncertainty and noise.
paragraphs: An estimation procedure turns measurement records into an inference about an unknown parameter. Precision depends both on how the signal changes the state and on how measurements extract that information.
Control can strengthen a useful response or suppress unwanted disturbances. However, the signal and noise may act through related physical mechanisms, making their separation a central issue.

sections.title: Noise-resilient quantum sensing
sections.summary: Quantum sensing protocols that retain sensitivity in the presence of decoherence and control errors.
paragraphs: Error suppression in sensing must preserve the parameter-dependent evolution that carries the signal. Error correction can help only under suitable conditions on the signal, noise, and available operations.
Another approach exploits enhanced response near critical behavior. Evaluating either strategy requires counting preparation and measurement time as well as noise and control overhead.
questions: Which experimentally available controls suppress noise without erasing the parameter being estimated?
Does an apparent precision gain survive preparation time, readout cost, and model uncertainty?

chapters.title: Quantum processor architectures
chapters.summary: System architectures for quantum computation, including qubit connectivity, control, readout, and classical processing.
paragraphs: A quantum processor architecture specifies qubit organization, interactions, control, readout, and classical processing. Connectivity, operation times, and error mechanisms constrain the computations that the system can implement.

Architecture research evaluates how these components support logical operations and error correction. Resource estimates must include ancillary qubits, routing, measurement, decoding, and control requirements, using assumptions consistent with the intended physical platform.

sections.title: Integrated fault-tolerant architectures
sections.summary: Integration of quantum error correction, logical operations, decoding, and real-time control.
paragraphs: Fault-tolerant architecture connects an error-correcting code to a physical layout, repeated measurements, decoding, and a schedule of logical operations. These layers must meet one another’s assumptions for the proposed protection to be meaningful.

Integration requires compatible resource and timing models across these components. Theoretical code performance, numerical models, and physical demonstrations provide different kinds of evidence and should remain distinguishable.
questions: How can readout, decoding, and conditional control meet the timing requirements of logical operations?
Which architecture tradeoffs remain favorable after routing, ancillary qubits, and calibration overhead are included?
